stages.name: Source
stages.what: The bytes the answer is made of, pinned so the same run can be repeated.

stages.name: Load & type
stages.what: Named tables in, typed frames out. The one interface the engine is allowed to depend on.

stages.name: Admission
stages.what: Does this data fit, is it sound, and what can it actually support? Answered before anything is computed.

stages.name: Extract
stages.what: The profile's own reading of the source: line-grain measures, document-grain measures, dimensions.

stages.name: Walk the chain
stages.what: The declared step chain, computed at the grain each measure is actually known at.

stages.name: Certify
stages.what: Which documents are fully decomposable, and the sentence explaining each that is not.

stages.name: Aggregate
stages.what: Roll up to any dimension the grain supports — and abstain, with a reason, where it does not.

stages.name: Contract
stages.what: The typed object Track B receives, re-checked against its own arithmetic before it is emitted.

stages.name: Models
stages.what: D4–D6. Fitted only where the readiness score says the data can carry them.

stages.name: Track
stages.what: The run, keyed to the hash of the data that produced it.

io: bytes on disk, pinned by DVC
source.note: The snapshot is an input the pipeline receives, not one it produces, so DVC pins its bytes rather than rebuilding it. The sha256 over these files travels all the way to the result object.

io:
DataFrame(1408 x 5)
quantity   int64
line_total float64
load.note: A CSV round-trip makes every column text. `_normalise` applies the profile's declared semantic types, so `list_price` is a number before anything compares it. Unparseable values become NaN, which the engine already treats as UNAVAILABLE rather than as zero.

io:
conformance EXACT
readiness 83.3 READY
0 blocking findings
admit.note: Three gates, cheapest first. Conformance asks whether the files match the profile at all; validation checks referential integrity and semantic types; readiness scores what the data can support. A dangling product reference stops the run here rather than producing a smaller book that looks fine.

extract.note: One join, once, up front. The line-grain measures are computed here; the order's two discount edges are read separately and deliberately left at order grain.

io:
facts  (line grain, 4 steps)
keys   (doc grain, 9 steps)
chain.note: The chain is walked twice: once at line grain for the steps knowable per line, then the line measures are summed up into the order and the rest of the chain runs there. Summing up needs no assumption. Dividing down would.

certify.note: A document is certified when every measure the chain needs is present and no discount edge has an unrecorded amount. 170 orders fail — 113 for a product with no unit cost, 60 for no list price, 11 for a discount whose amount nobody wrote down. Each carries the sentence that says which.

io:
one row per group
+ coverage_pct
+ grain_note
aggregate.note: Coverage is 75.71% — 530 of 700 orders — and it is printed beside the total rather than behind it. A step is summed only when every contributing row has it, so a partial sum can never masquerade as a result.

contract.note: `contracts.validate()` re-derives the arithmetic it can check — invoice price must equal gross minus on-invoice, pocket must equal invoice minus leakage — and rejects the payload if it does not reconcile. It also refuses any COMPLETE record that cites no evidence.

models.note: The headline waterfall does not go through the model layer. Segmentation, elasticity and price recommendation read the same fact tables but produce different records.

io:
totals, flags, availability,
the result JSON
track.note: MLflow records the run; DVC records the bytes. They meet at the snapshot hash, so given a run you can recover the exact data, and given the data you can regenerate the run.

source.note: Look closely at the columns. The edge carries a transaction, a discount and an amount. There is no product on it. That single absence is the whole of this trace.

load.note: An amount that is blank stays NaN rather than becoming zero. The engine keeps three states apart: no edge at all (a true zero), an edge with no amount (unknown), and a field never populated (a gap).

io:
WARNING discount amounts:
15 applied with unknown amount
admit.note: Validation flags this as a warning, not a blocker — it degrades a result without invalidating it, and it travels into the confidence reasons on the contract record.

extract.note: This is the function where the pro-rata allocation used to live. It returned the discount against each line, split in proportion to line value. It now returns it against the order and stops.

chain.note: `propagate_grain` computes this once from the chain. A level built from a line-grain level and an order-grain deduction is knowable only at order grain, and so is everything below it — including pocket margin, even though COGS is a line-grain measure.

certify.note: Certification is unaffected: it asks whether the inputs are present, not where they can be reported.

io:
product_id  on_invoice_discount
PRD-001                  NaN
PRD-002                  NaN
aggregate.note: `product` is not constant inside an order, so the groupby reads the line frame — where the order-grain columns do not exist at all. A column that exists is a column someone will sum, so they are not there to be summed.

contract.note: The reason travels with the null. Track B can write the sentence "we cannot attribute this discount to a product" instead of inferring something from a blank.

track.note: Per-step availability is logged on every run, so a drop in what the book can report shows up as a metric rather than as a surprise in a meeting.

io:
the mapping is a schema,
the workbook is the data
source.note: The mapping arrived before the workbook did, so `make_mapping_fixture.py` runs the mapping backwards and generates a workbook with exactly the structure it declares. Every value in it is a placeholder; the sheets, columns and resolving keys are real.

load.note: The profile asks for `financial_plan`; the mapping resolves that to sheet `24_Financial_Plan`. That indirection is what lets one engine read a CSV snapshot and a client's workbook without knowing the difference.

io:
waterfall        READY
segmentation   BLOCKED
elasticity     BLOCKED
optimisation   BLOCKED
admit.note: A good score cannot buy a READY. The mapping records no customer and no date on the plan sheet, so three of five deliverables are impossible here — and the score says so before anything is fitted rather than after something crashes.

io:
one fact row per
scenario x SKU x region
extract.note: The plan row is the finest grain at which this mapping exposes any amount. `23_Invoices` maps InvoiceLine ids and links and not one measure; `08_Products` exposes `SKU_ID` and nothing else, so there is no list price anywhere.

chain.note: A different chain, the same engine. Four canonical steps — list value, negotiated off-list, on-invoice discount, invoice price — are simply absent, because the mapping cannot support them. Because the key is the row, nothing ever abstains for grain here.

certify.note: Every measure the chain needs is present on every row, so the whole plan is decomposable. Compare the CSV snapshot's 75.7%: a shorter chain is easier to satisfy, which is a fact about the chain rather than about the data quality.

aggregate.note: Every dimension the dairy profile declares is constant within a plan row, so the product slice reports all five steps. The engine also reconciles the result against the sheet's own `Planned_Contribution_Margin_SAR` — agreement to 2e-11.

contract.note: The same `EngineResult` Track B already reads. The steps this mapping cannot support come back as UNAVAILABLE carrying "no list price is mapped on any sheet; 08_Products exposes SKU_ID only" — a sentence someone can act on upstream.

io:
segmentation  BLOCKED
elasticity    BLOCKED
optimisation  BLOCKED
models.note: Readiness is consulted first rather than caught afterwards. Running the fit and handling the exception would reach the same place, but it would reach it by accident and the reason would be a traceback rather than a sentence.

track.note: Change the mapping and the same workbook is a different read, so the provenance hash covers both.
